title: Block impossible calendar dates in delta checks
source: lib/ohworks-delta-check.ts:290-295 and :322-327 rely on Date.parse alone; :307-308 grants no-prior pass. Inline reproduction: current capturedAt=2026-02-30T12:00:00Z with valid rules and prior=null returns pass/no-prior-result. prompt:
Reject impossible calendar dates before evaluating synthetic result deltas. lib/ohworks-delta-check.ts:290-295 and :322-327 rely on Date.parse plus a finiteness check. JavaScript normalizes February 30 into March instead of rejecting it. With otherwise valid identity, value, units, and rules, a current capturedAt of 2026-02-30T12:00:00Z and prior=null reproduced a pass/no-prior-result at lines 307-308. The same normalization can incorrectly place a prior result inside or outside a comparison window.

Add a local timestamp validation helper that checks the literal ISO calendar fields, including leap years and month lengths, before using the parsed instant. Apply it to both current and prior timestamps. Return the existing current-timestamp-invalid or prior-timestamp-invalid block outcome for impossible dates. Preserve valid explicit-offset ISO timestamps as well as Z timestamps; avoid introducing a UTC-only restriction or a shared helper that expands the file scope. Keep comparison windows and threshold rules unchanged.

Extend tests/ohworks/delta-check.test.ts with impossible dates in both positions, a non-leap February 29, a valid leap day, and a valid offset timestamp. Include the no-prior reproduction and assert the existing reason codes. Run node --import tsx --test tests/ohworks/delta-check.test.ts. work on the assigned branch you are on. Use fabricated data and edit only the allowed files; no merges, rebases, commits, pushes, authentication changes, database work, or external operations.
